title: Aligned reads and FASTQ lane/library information

latest.raw:
Hi organizers, thanks for running the hackathon.

I checked the dataset README and the existing discussions, including [the reference-genome thread](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SageBio/rare-disease-real-kid-mva-hackathon-2026/discussions/17) and [the phase/parental-transmission question](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SageBio/rare-disease-real-kid-mva-hackathon-2026/discussions/24). I have two separate practical questions before planning local read alignment:

1. Are aligned, indexed BAM/CRAM files available to registered participants under the existing controlled-access arrangement, or should we work from the FASTQs?
2. Do the four FASTQ pairs represent different lanes/libraries of the same sample? Is sequencing platform, library preparation and expected fragment/insert-size information available?

If this is documented elsewhere, a link would be much appreciated. I'm asking only about the supplied sequencing resources, not additional clinical records.

Thank you!

latest.raw:
Hi Donvitocorleone,

Thanks for checking the existing discussions first ,  really appreciate it.

1) BAM/CRAM: Not currently available under the controlled-access arrangement — only the raw FASTQs are provided, so you'll need to align locally. Reference genome is GRCh38.

2) Sequencing platform / library prep: Illumina DNA PCR-Free Prep, sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq.

On whether the four FASTQ pairs represent different lanes/libraries of the same sample, and expected fragment/insert-size — I don't have that confirmed on my end. Let me check with the team and follow up with specifics

Best,
Gaia
